citation.title: Progress and plan of KSTAR plasma control system upgrade
citation.authors: Hahn, S.-h.; Kim, Y.J.; Penaflor, B.G.; et al.

topic: KSTAR plasma control system status through 2014 and the hardware/OS upgrade plan for 2015-2016.
own_question: What the KSTAR PCS can do and how its real-time hardware and software should be upgraded for advanced scenarios.
actual_method_and_evidence: This is an engineering status report. It describes magnetic, vertical-stability and kinetic controls: beta-p PID with NBI, density PID, and preliminary ECCD/NTM work. It also reports a testbed loopback test of new AI/AO hardware under MRG-R Linux, with tabulated latency for a 20-100 kHz cycle. The paper has no CES, ion temperature, BES/ECEI or nowcasting content. The real-time Te-profile feedback is listed only as a desired future theme.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: The KSTAR PCS has used real-time feedback for kinetic quantities. Examples are beta-p control using NBI power and line-averaged density control.
claim_checks.qualification: These results are from 2012-2014 and come from the authors' summary. They concern electron density and magnetics-based beta-p, not ion temperature from CES.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: The paper does not cover CES timing. The latency figures belong to the loopback hardware test only and are unrelated to our 10 ms grid.
validation_if_relevant: There is a hardware latency test on a testbed. There is no plasma-data validation relevant to our study.
forbidden_inferences: Do not claim that KSTAR uses CES Ti in real-time control.
Do not treat the planned Te feedback as achieved.
Do not cite the loopback latency as our computation time or as evidence of deployment feasibility.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Use at most as optional context that KSTAR has a real-time PCS with kinetic feedback, which motivates the optional application framing. It does not support our nowcasting claims.
source_scope_note: All extracted page texts supplied; figure/equation visual validation remains separate
